h: Finding your favourites in a giant museum
p: With so many floors, the Science Museum works best with a loose plan. Little ones aged up to about seven often make a beeline for the play-focused spaces, while older kids and teens tend to love Wonderlab: The Equinor Gallery, a ticketed interactive gallery full of experiments, demonstrations and live shows. It's well worth the extra cost if your family enjoys getting hands-on.

For the history buffs, look out for the Apollo 10 command module, which carried astronauts around the Moon in 1969 as a dress rehearsal for the first landing, and Puffing Billy, one of the oldest surviving steam locomotives in the world. The Medicine galleries are fascinating too, tracing how people have tried to heal the body over the centuries.

The museum has its own IMAX cinema, so you can round off a visit with a big-screen documentary. Adults without kids in tow should look out for the Science Museum Lates, evening events for over-18s with talks, activities and a lively atmosphere.

A tip for busy days: the museum is huge, so agree on a meeting point if your group splits up. Eat early or late to dodge the lunchtime rush, and don't feel you have to see everything. Plenty of families come back again and again, ticking off a new gallery each time.
